brent-barham-community-library.lastSummary: The council listing describes a volunteer-run library and a knitting/sewing group, with contact details and a provider link. brent-bias-active-ageing.lastSummary: Council and provider content support the named Irish community organisation and its Active Ageing social activities. brent-black-girls-do-run.lastSummary: The provider confirms free North West London social running, beginners welcome, and joining through its next-run/Heylo route. The next session and individual accessibility still need checking; a phone contact was not published in the material read.

brent-brondesbury-park-synagogue.name: Brondesbury Park United Synagogue
brent-brondesbury-park-synagogue.lastSummary: Brent Council describes the named modern Orthodox Jewish community, welcoming younger and older people and families, and publishes the matching telephone number. brent-carers-centre.lastSummary: The provider describes support for unpaid adult and young carers in Brent. brent-changing-mindsets.lastSummary: The provider describes a lived-experience-led Brent mental wellbeing group, membership enquiries and members-only Wellbeing Thursdays, consistent with the listing. brent-citizens-advice.lastSummary: The provider helplines page supports Brent-resident eligibility for the local information and guidance line, the listed phone and Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 10am–4pm hours. It also links to online requests and face-to-face Brent hub advice. The page describes money/debt and Universal Credit routes. brent-club-brent-sport.lastSummary: The provider programme page supports adapted multi-sport at Willesden Sports Centre, the explicit age range of eight and over, involvement of carers and siblings, online booking, and the listed £4 term-time sessions. Current spaces and individual support requirements are not confirmed; the listing advises checking before booking.

brent-cove.name: Brent Cove
brent-cove.lastSummary: Hestia supports the listed Brent-resident age eligibility, listening/crisis support, appointment-free drop-in and daily 2pm–10pm opening. No changed crisis contact is proposed or reproduced.

brent-crisis-fund.lastSummary: The council supports the fund purpose, adult Brent residency, savings rules, online application, Hub assistance and listed phone. Propose clarifying the application limit and partner rule. Awards remain discretionary; individual entitlement cannot be confirmed.

brent-cycletastic.lastSummary: Official indexed provider content supports the volunteer-led repair project, free learn-to-fix sessions, booking email and relocation to Clitterhouse Farm. brent-cycling-campaign.name: Brent Cycling Campaign
brent-cycling-campaign.lastSummary: Council content supports local cycling advocacy, rides, social events and contact through its published email/provider link. brent-diya.name: Diya — South Asian peer support
brent-diya.lastSummary: Provider content supports South Asian peer support for Harrow and Brent residents experiencing mental health challenges, free sessions in Harrow and direct contact to enquire. brent-elders-voice-activities.lastSummary: Provider content supports singing, art and movement activities for Brent residents over 55, with a retirees drop-in for over 65s. brent-granville-community-kitchen.lastSummary: Council content supports the South Kilburn community food hub, food-related activities and matching phone. brent-libraries.lastSummary: Council lists Brent libraries, books, computer and study bookings, activities and online joining. The page links to charges but does not give all activity prices or individual availability.

brent-hubs.lastSummary: Council describes free help with housing, benefits, work, food and digital skills, with different local hubs and drop-in arrangements. Individual eligibility and availability were not confirmed.

queue.name: Black Girls Do Run UK — North West London
queue.currentValue: Black women and women of colour, including people new to running.
queue.proposedValue: Black women and women of colour aged 18 and over, including people new to running.
queue.reason: Include the explicit minimum age stated on the local programme page so callers can check suitability before joining.
queue.evidence: The North West London programme describes encouraging Black women aged 18 and over to run and welcomes people just starting out.

queue.name: Brent Resident Support Fund — crisis payment
queue.currentValue: Evidence required. Normally one application per rolling 12 months, even if a previous application was declined. Awards are discretionary.
queue.proposedValue: Evidence required. One application per rolling 12 months, even if declined. For couples, an application by either partner counts towards this limit; it does not apply to other adult household members. Awards are discretionary.
queue.reason: The council states a firm rolling application limit and explicitly applies it to couples; the listing omits the partner rule and says normally.
queue.evidence: One application is allowed in a rolling 12 months, approved or rejected. A partner application during that period is declined; other adults in the household are not included in this partner restriction.
